images.title: The diagonals of a rectangle meet at their middles
images.purpose: Shows rectangle ABCD whose 8 cm diagonals cross at O, cutting each other into four 4 cm halves.
images.composition: Plain white background, the main object large and centred with wide empty margins, no scenery, no characters, no extra decoration. One large rectangle in the centre with its two diagonals drawn and the four equal halves marked.
images.exact_structure: One rectangle ABCD in dark outline, wider than it is tall (about 3 by 2), with A top left, B top right, C bottom right and D bottom left. The two diagonals AC and BD are drawn as thick teal (#0072B2) lines and cross at the point O, marked with a small filled reddish purple (#CC79A7) dot. Each of the four half diagonals OA, OB, OC and OD carries exactly one short amber (#E69F00) tick mark, the same on all four, showing they are equal. The label 4 cm sits beside half diagonal OA and the label 4 cm beside half diagonal OB. The letters A, B, C, D sit outside their corners and O sits just below the crossing point. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: The diagonals of a rectangle are equal and cut each other in half, so each half is 4 cm.
images.description: Shows rectangle ABCD whose 8 cm diagonals cross at O, cutting each other into four 4 cm halves.
images.context: AC = BD = 8 cm, so OA = OB = OC = OD = 8 ÷ 2 = 4 cm (AAS on ∆AOB and ∆COD).

image_decisions.why: The four equal halves at the crossing show the bisecting property and the answer 4 cm at a glance.
